page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with two Hebrew phrases inline. No margin notes. Below the last line, the catchword "Epho" stands at the right.

main_text.p: ke [?] nuperus autor est. Idem eodem modo colligit Pater tuus Cap. 20. comment. Maforet. Censor meus ex eodem loco aliud mihi imponebat, Ephodæum Maforam improbasse, sed oculis ira fascinatis, eorum quæ asserui, nihil videre potuit.

9. Ex eadem pag. De sensu contendis libri Cozri eo loco. Ego sane assentiri tibi non possum. Longiori sermone opus est, quam ferat epistola. Paucis dicam. Duo sunt controversiæ nostræ capita. De sensu verborum unum, alterum de autoris mente & scopo in hac disputatione: In utroque, parte verbis meis, toto cælo aberrare mihi videris, ut ego tibi. Quod ad prius attinet, illud כדברי רובה qvod interpretatus sum in re damnabili, tu vero in re debita & honesta, pater tuus interpretatur, in re culpabili & inutili. Sic intellexit commentator Cozri, ut ex adnotatione ad illa verba. במושהיו רבים מזנים [illegible, ~2 letters] multi fuerunt ejusmodi vituperantes opus & industriam eorum. Quod probat ex Epho

page.notes: The "c" at the top right corner and the dark mark at the top right edge are not printed text and are left out. "ke" at the start of the first line is unclear. The Hebrew phrase in the second line has a gap of about two letters that I could not read; the letters after it appear to be עניכם. The first Hebrew phrase, כדברי רובה, is read from the scan. The catchword "Epho" is the start of the next page.
